question: Does any M-77 / Parpola text-no.-7 object or string identity survive source normalization?
decision: The three-sign BASE_T graphic string survives, but the two seal identifiers printed by Parpola 2019 do not. CISI M-35 has seven signs and CISI M-77 has five. CISI M-37 is the source-visible three-sign seal that graphically matches text no. 7 without final sign 107, and the Lipi and Mayig machine layers concordantly encode M-37 as the same three-position string. M-37 is therefore a high-confidence intended-reference correction candidate, not an author-confirmed emendation.

parpola_standardized_strings.U: The first sign in reading order is visible in Figure 1 but is not numbered in the checked 2019 prose. No number is assigned here.

rejected_identities.source_result: CISI, Lipi, and Mayig all show seven signs
CISI, Lipi, and Mayig all show five signs

correction_candidate.reason: M-37 alone is a complete three-sign seal whose CISI impression matches the standardized BASE_T graphic sequence; Lipi and Mayig agree on its three positions.
